title: Emerging Technology Weekly Briefing
description: Quantum and post-quantum cryptography, robotics and autonomy, advanced compute, and space-enabled tech.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 20–28. New: Google Cloud said Oct. 27 that Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is in public preview. No new space-system award was found. No post-quantum announcement newer than the Oct. 26 AWS ML-KEM note was found. NVIDIA's Oct. 27 Vera Rubin availability on Oracle Cloud is on the data-center page.

items.headline: AWS Key Management Service adds ML-KEM for post-quantum key encapsulation
items.summary: AWS said Oct. 26 that Key Management Service now supports Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism, ML-KEM, which it identifies as the NIST FIPS 203 standard meant to replace Diffie-Hellman, elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman and RSA key transport. AWS says the point is the harvest-now, decrypt-later risk, in which an adversary records a key exchange today and recovers it once a quantum computer can. KMS supports ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024. AWS says the private key stays in FIPS 140-3 Level 3 hardware security modules, and that the feature is available in every KMS region except the Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain) and China regions.

items.headline: Google Cloud puts Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 in public preview
items.summary: Google Cloud said Oct. 27 that Gemini Robotics Embodied Reasoning 2 is in public preview on the Gemini platform. Google describes it as a model that works across robot bodies, from stationary arms to humanoids, and that combines spatial and temporal video understanding with long-horizon planning and safety guardrails. Google says developers can declare low-level controls, including vision-language-action models and navigation APIs, as tools, and can test behaviors in MuJoCo-Warp and NVIDIA Isaac Sim before using hardware. Boston Dynamics' Marco da Silva said the model changes what an inspection with Spot can be, because applying models to video lets the robot do more than check a single moment.

items.headline: NVIDIA's Isaac update adds a reference humanoid and Isaac Lab 3.0
items.summary: At GTC Berlin on Oct. 21 NVIDIA expanded the Isaac open robotics platform with a reference humanoid, datasets, a runtime, and a learning-framework update. Agile Robots' Agile ONE SN uses Isaac GR00T and Jetson Thor, with Halos safety integration planned. Isaac OS and Isaac Lab 3.0 are part of the release, along with reference workflows that use ChatGPT Astra, Isaac and Cosmos on DGX Station. NVIDIA described the release as a commercial robotics platform.

items.headline: TorchTPU makes Google TPUs a native PyTorch target
items.summary: Google open-sourced TorchTPU on Oct. 20, co-developed with Meta's PyTorch team. The company says training, serving and deployment on TPUs can use the existing PyTorch tools, including vLLM, Hugging Face and TorchTitan, instead of a separate stack. Google's stated change is portability: PyTorch code can target TPUs without a separate software stack.

items.headline: Dell announces Vera CPU servers aimed at agent orchestration, separate from GPU racks
items.summary: At GTC Berlin, Dell said the PowerEdge M9882 packs 256 NVIDIA Vera CPUs into a 48U rack for agent work such as orchestration, tool use, code execution and evaluation, next to GPU racks used for inference. The air-cooled PowerEdge R8822 is a two-socket Vera server for standard 19-inch racks, with support for up to four double-wide GPUs. Dell says the M9882 is due in the first quarter of calendar 2027 and the R8822 this month. The point of the split is to stop over-provisioning mixed servers when the agent loop is CPU-heavy.
